themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 344% increase (z-score: 6.46)—suggesting a potential public health or sanitation breakdown in Parkchester/Soundview this week.
evidence: 5 dead animal complaints filed this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (344% spike)
Z-score of 6.46 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
No recent Reddit or local news coverage suggests story is breaking now
reporting_angles: Call DSNY and DOH to determine if there's a documented rat die-off, disease vector spike, or disposal crisis
Interview residents in affected blocks to map specific locations and frequency; ask about rodent activity patterns

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 5 this week compared to 0.9 per week baseline—a 471% spike (z-score: 5.28)—raising questions about industrial emissions, construction dust, or traffic pollution in this week's data.
evidence: 5 air quality complaints filed this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (471% spike)
Z-score of 5.28 indicates statistically extreme deviation
396 DOB permits on file including 46 new buildings and 294 alterations may indicate construction-related dust sources
reporting_angles: Cross-reference air quality complaints with active DOB construction permits; identify which sites residents cited
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to check for air monitoring data and any enforcement actions this week
Interview residents with respiratory complaints to understand timeframe and suspected sources

themes_detail.label: Encampment Expansion
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 3 complaints two weeks ago versus 0.2 per week baseline—a 1100% spike (z-score: 4.16)—coinciding with repeated community board budget requests for homeless services expansion and street outreach.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike)
Z-score of 4.16 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Community board has submitted repeated annual budget requests for 'Expand street outreach' and 'Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' to DHS—unmet demand signal
reporting_angles: Map the 3 encampments from 2-week-ago complaints; conduct field reporting on current conditions and displacement patterns
Interview DHS about street outreach resource allocation in CD 209 and why repeated budget requests remain unfunded
Speak with community board members about year-over-year requests and resource gaps; contextualize against city-wide homelessness trends

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 4 this week versus 0.9 per week baseline—a 357% increase (z-score: 4.0)—potentially linked to inadequate park infrastructure and programming, another recurring community board budget gap.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints filed this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% spike)
Z-score of 4.0 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community board has standing request to 'Provide a new, or new expansion to, a building in a park' (DPR)—suggests parks infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated the 4 complaints this week; visit to assess noise sources and enforcement response
Interview Parks Dept about park programming, security staffing, and event scheduling in Parkchester/Soundview
Ask community board why park infrastructure requests are perennial; gather resident testimony on unmet recreational needs

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints tripled to 10 this week from a 3.0 per week baseline—a 233% spike (z-score: 2.98)—suggesting either an uptick in unlicensed or problematic street vending activity this week.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints filed this week vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (233% spike)
Z-score of 2.98 indicates statistically significant anomaly
311 data shows spike is acute this week, not a sustained trend
reporting_angles: Obtain NYPD/DOC vendor complaint details to identify block patterns and vendor types (food, merchandise, etc.)
Check for recent policy changes, enforcement sweeps, or seasonal vendor surge
Interview street vendors and residents to understand root cause of spike and community tolerance
